why: Simulate the days, but keep the right bookkeeping: every server with id replaced[j] changes at once, so only how many servers carry each id matters. Keep a count per id plus a running total; each day moves a whole bucket from the old id to the new id in O(1).
hints: All servers with the same id are replaced together. Do you ever need to tell two servers with the same id apart?
No: keep count[id] and total = sum(id * count[id]). A replacement moves count[old] servers to new, changing total by (new - old) * count[old].
Counter of server ids, then one O(1) update per day and append the total. O(n) overall instead of O(n^2) for rewriting the array daily.
pitfalls: If replaced[j] is not present that day, nothing changes but you still report the total.
When replaced[j] == newId[j], do not delete the bucket after adding to it; handle that case (or update in an order that is safe).
Merging buckets: after day 1 of example 1 every server is 20, so the next replacement of 20 moves both servers.
